# Security

- SEC-008 (should): An app never stores passwords or issues its own access tokens: users sign in with an OpenID Connect provider (Microsoft Entra ID or Entra External ID unless an ADR picks another), and an HTTP API accepts its access tokens with AddJwtBearer, which checks their signature, issuer, audience and lifetime, set under Authentication:Schemes:Bearer; development uses dotnet user-jwts, whose key stays in user secrets; ASP.NET Core Identity or any other scheme needs an ADR.
- SEC-018 (must): Don't generate your own access tokens or ID tokens, except for testing purposes; use OpenID Connect or an OAuth standard to create access tokens for API access, and you should not create an access token from a username and password request. JWT bearer tokens should be fully validated in an API (signature, issuer, audience and expiration), and the API should return 401 when any of them is incorrect. ASVS 9.1.1, 9.2.1 and 9.2.3 ask for the signature or MAC, validity time span and audience checks.
